newsitem.title: USA: North Dakotans prepare for record river crest.
newsitem.headline: North Dakotans prepare for record river crest.

text.p: Thousands of college students joined sandbagging efforts Thursday ahead of the expected record crest of the Red River.
The river was forecast to crest at 39.5 feet, which could have water spilling over some sandbagged levees that now range from 38.5 to 39 feet, said emergency personnel.
Frigid temperatures have slowed the river's rise and created ice jams that made it difficult to estimate when the river would crest.
"We are anticipating it today, but it could be anytime after that," said Captain Pat Richards of North Dakota's Emergency Management Division.

In Fargo and Moorehead, thousands of students from North Dakota State University and Moorhead State University planned to join flood volunteers, as both schools will be closed on Thursday so students, faculty and staff can help with sandbagging efforts.
Carbon monoxide poisoning claimed one life and sickened about two dozen others as widespread power outages caused residents to use portable generators.
A La Moure County, North Dakota, a man was found dead in his farm shop, where a generator was running. The local sheriff said Robert Schweigert, 46, died while trying to leave the shop.
"There are cases reported where they are operating in attached garages, and the resulting fumes are getting back in the homes and causing people to become very, very ill," said Richards.

The Minnesota Highway Patrol said a woman and her daughter died from exposure after escaping an accident in which their car washed into a creek. A total of eight people have died in the past two weeks of flooding and snowstorms in the United States and and Canada.
In Minnesota, the Minnesota River was forecast to crest this weekend near Minneapolis, prompting continued sandbagging efforts South of the city where flooding has already closed roads and highways.
